newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 16.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- The U.N. Security Council adopts a presidential statement expressing concern over the intrusion of a North Korean submarine into the South, calling for Pyongyang to abide by the armistice agreement.
- International oil prices are on a sharp upswing, reaching $22 per barrel.
- POSCO begins construction of fifth blast furnace. It is expected to become the world's no.1 steelmaker by 1999.

- North Korea asks U.S. to provide an official explanation on the results of a recent visit to South Korea by Assistant Secretary of State Winston Lord. It claims that linking the submarine intrusion incident to talks between Washington and Pyongyang is unreasonable.
- The United Nations Security Council was prepared to adopt a presidential statement expressing concern over the intrusion of a North Korean submarine into South Korea.
- State prosecutors demanded prison terms of up to six years for 62 militant students who were indicted for illegal, violent demonstrations on and around Yonsei University campus.
- U.S. Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole demanded that President Bill Clinton answer questions about his links to Asian businessmen and their contributions to Democratic party coffers.
